La Petite Ecole Française
Bilingual French/English School in London
Nursery and Primary open for all
La Petite Ecole Française
Nurturing Happy Children
La Petite Ecole (established 1983) is a bilingual Nursery and Primary school in Notting Hill, teaching in English and French. The school has a reputation for excellence and is consistently placed amongst the best bilingual schools in London. We pride ourselves on our small class sizes and personalised approach to teaching. We are an inclusive and secular school.
La Petite Ecole is a nurturing and homely environment in which children thrive. We believe that every child is an individual with unique talents. Our aim is to create an environment that allows the child to flourish both academically and creatively. We strive to develop confident and happy children.
Free Early Years funding (15 or 30 hours/week) for all pupils under 5 years old, unless fees are paid by employer or Bourse.
School Opening Times: Mon-Fri 9-3:30pm, Wed 9-12:30pm.
Small class sizes
Clubs and wrap-around services
Internationally Accredited
Internationally Accredited
The school has been awarded ‘Homologation’ status (special accreditation from the French Ministry of Education AEFE) and our pupils can progress onto French or English schools. This means you can rest assured that the highest standards are consistently being met.
Our wonderful parent community is International and includes non-French speaking families looking for high quality bilingual education in central London, with access to the best secondary schools.

Bilingual Foundations That Last a Lifetime
Early Bilingual Learning at La Petite École Française
At our school, bilingual learning is not an additional feature. It is woven into the heart of everything we do. From the earliest years, children learn through both English and French in a natural, joyful and immersive way.
Our teachers are experts in early childhood education and bilingual development. Lessons flow naturally between both languages through songs, stories, conversation, projects and structured activities. By engaging with two languages daily, children develop strong communication skills and a flexible approach to learning.
The Science Behind Bilingual Benefits
Research in neuroscience shows that bilingual children develop enhanced problem solving, better concentration and stronger memory. Their brains become skilled at switching between tasks and absorbing new information. We see these benefits often and enjoy sharing them with families through our parent friendly workshops.
We welcome children from French, British and international backgrounds, including many who speak neither French nor English at home. Our supportive and nurturing atmosphere helps each child develop confidence in both languages, regardless of their starting point.
Preparing Children for the Future
Our AEFE accreditation ensures that children receive a globally respected education that prepares them for the next stage, whether they continue in the French or British system. Our pupils regularly move into top schools in London and abroad with the strong academic and language foundation they need to succeed.
A Place Where Children Grow and Shine
Our spacious outdoor areas provide children with opportunities for physical development, exploration and imaginative play. Outdoor learning promotes wellbeing and complements the structured teaching in our classrooms.
At La Petite École Française, we are proud to offer an education that balances academic excellence with warmth, creativity and emotional wellbeing. Our bilingual setting gives children a powerful head start and a joyful foundation for future learning.

Parents’ Involvement
Information and Communication Technologies
Nursery and Primary open for all
La Petite Ecole Française
Parents’ Involvement
At La Petite Ecole Française we strive to create a ‘family’ atmosphere by involving the parents as much as possible throughout the year. The teachers are approachable and regular dialogue and communication between the parents and staff is encouraged.
Within weeks of the school commencing, the parents are invited to visit the school, meet the teachers and learn how the school operates. Topics covered include important information such as the curriculum for the year as well as more mundane issues such as what to give at snack time and naturally, parents are encouraged to ask questions. During the course of the year there are regular events such as the Science Day, reading stories in their own langage, Christmas Carols, the World Book Day… parties to which the parents are invited. We also invite parents to help us organizing the School Fair at the end of the year.
If a parent has any concerns and would like to talk about a problem or the progress of a child, they can arrange an afterschool meeting with the class teacher or the head teacher.
If parents have any concerns or feedback about the school which they would like to raise with the Department for Education (schools inspectorate) here are the contact details:

Department for Education (DfE)
Online contact: www.gov.uk/government/organisation/department-for-education
The school is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).

pageCache.text:
Bilingual Curriculum and Activities
Bilingual French/English School in London
Our Teachers and Classes
We Are Passionate About Teaching
The school has excellent teachers who are enthusiastic, motivated and passionate about teaching. The teachers are supported by class assistants.
In addition to the regular classes, the children have weekly dance lessons (expression corporelle), music lessons, English lessons, Spanish lessons (primary level) and sports lessons that are conducted by specialist teachers in small groups of 9 children.
During these times, the rest of the class remains with the regular teacher and benefits from a more personalised lesson in which each child’s area of weakness can be addressed.
Small Class Sizes
We pride ourselves on our small class sizes and a personalised approach to teaching. Children learn best in small groups, so our Maternelle (Nursery to Year 1) class sizes have a maximum of 18 pupils with a teacher and assistant teacher.
The older classes have a maximum of 20 pupils with a teacher. When the children do specialised lessons such as dance, music or English the classes are split further into small groups of 9. Learning and activities take place in small groups, ensuring that the pupils get more one-to-one time with the teacher.
The Best Start for your Child
English Lessons - A Bilingual Approach
In Maternelle (Nursery to Year 1) 40% of lessons are taught in English. This will increase to 50% by September 2025. From Year 2 onwards, 25% of teaching time is conducted in English in small groups.
All our English teachers are native English speakers. They teach English grammar and literacy but also cultural aspects and topics within the French curriculum.
Due to the small English classes and excellent teaching, pupils who have been with the school since Maternelle leave in CM2 as fully bilingual students and can progress on to English or French schools.
Extra Curricular Activities and Wrap-Around Care
We know that parents are very busy with work commitments and are looking for a school that offers wrap-around care and after school clubs. We have a Garderie in the morning from 8am until school starts as well as from 3.30pm until 5pm. La Petite Ecole Française offers a wide range of after school clubs depending on the age of the pupil and his/her interest. These include, Coding, Science. Gardening, Music, Drama, Capoeira (Brazilian Martial Arts), Art club, English, Football, Rugby and so on.
The list of after school clubs is communicated to the parents before the beginning of each term. More information, for example on timetable and price, can be provided by the school office or the after school club teacher who directly organises each activity.
The Science Behind the Benefits of Bilingualism
This BBC video (Lee please link to the BBC page) explains why being bilingual at an early age increases the development of neural networks and has long term benefits for the brain. Learning new languages exercises the mind. It improves our concentration, problem solving, memory and concentration. It can delay the onset of dementia and lead to quicker recovery from a stroke. The best time to learn a new language is when you are a child and building neural networks. It is a wonderful gift for any parent to give their child to broaden their opportunities in life.

Read about the school’s application process, how to apply, fees, and what happens next.

Curriculum
Bilingual French/English School in London
Nursery and Primary open for all
La Petite Ecole Française
Accredited by the French Ministry of Education
La Petite Ecole Française is a French nursery and primary school in London accredited by the French Ministry of Education. The curriculum taught at the school follows the official French curriculum. Every year, the French Inspector inspects the school to ensure that the school curriculum and methods of teaching conforms to the official syllabus and meets the necessary standards.
More information about the French curriculum can be found at: Programmes de l’Education Nationale
Academic Progress
French National Assessments (Évaluations nationales) are taken by pupils in specific year groups across the French education system. They help teachers understand pupils’ progress in key areas of learning by identifying strengths and areas where additional support may be needed. The results are used to plan teaching effectively and ensure all pupils continue to make good progress.The CM2 French National Assessment results for September 2025 show that our pupils achieved very strong outcomes compared with other AEFE network schools worldwide and the national average in France. These assessments are taken across AEFE schools in different international regions, allowing comparison between similar school contexts. ZENOS is the group of AEFE schools in Northern and Western Europe used as a regional comparator.

pageCache.text:
English Lessons
Bilingual French/English School in London
Nursery and Primary open for all
La Petite Ecole Française
Excellence in Tailor-Made Bilingual Education
At La Petite Ecole Française, excellence is at the core of our bilingual program. We provide our students with enhanced English immersion, offering a reinforced timetable compared to the standard French curriculum.
Our native English-speaking teachers follow the British curriculum while also integrating key subjects from the French program—such as history, geography, and science—into their English lessons. This unique and dynamic approach enables students to learn English in an engaging and natural environment.
Our tailor-made curriculum blends the best of the British and French education systems. From nursery school, children benefit from 50/50 English and French, preparing them for a truly International education. In the primary school, English is taught in small groups, ensuring individualised attention and a personalized learning experience that fosters linguistic excellence.Through our immersive and rigorous approach, our students develop authentic and lasting bilingualism, opening doors to top English and French schools.
Nursery - Immersion from an Early Age
At La Petite Ecole Française, we provide our youngest learners with true bilingual immersion from the very start of their education from Nursery to Year 1 (PS to Grande Section). With a 50-50 bilingual program, children are taught alternately by an English-speaking teacher and a French-speaking teacher, ensuring balanced exposure to both languages.
Our approach to learning English is engaging and interactive, inspired by the British curriculum and incorporating the Phonics program, allowing children to start reading and writing in English from Reception (Moyenne Section). Our English-speaking teachers, who are trained in EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage), use a play-based methodology to help children absorb the language naturally. They work closely with the French teacher and are supported by an assistant to provide personalised teaching.
We emphasize project-based learning, with diverse themes that spark curiosity and foster a love of learning. In addition, we promote cultural awareness, encouraging children to explore different cultures around the world to develop their intercultural sensitivity and their understanding of an International environment. In this rich and stimulating bilingual setting, our students build a strong foundation in both English and French.
Encouraging development
Primary - small classes with a personalised approach
At La Petite Ecole Française, English learning in primary school is part of a rich and immersive educational approach. Our students follow the British curriculum in reading, writing, and literature, building strong skills in comprehension and written expression.
To further enhance their learning, our teachers incorporate key elements of the French curriculum in history, geography, and science, following a program that has been carefully designed by both English and French speaking teachers. This blended approach allows students to develop not only a high level of English proficiency but also a deep understanding of the cultural and academic foundations of both the British and French education systems.
Thanks to the small group lessons the teaching is highly effective. This format enables teachers to challenge each student to reach their full potential, while also providing personalised support to those who need it.
Through this structured bilingual environment, our students continue to grow with confidence and excellence, strengthening their bilingualism and broadening their global perspective.

About La Petite Ecole Française
Bilingual French/English School in London
Family and Community, as well as a first class bilingual education, are the heart of our school.
La Petite Ecole Française
The Best Start for your Children
Based in Notting Hill London, the school caters for around 140 children from the age of 2 to 11. Entry is non-selective and we welcome non-French speakers.
Pupils leave the school fully bilingual and can progress on to French schools such as the Lycée Français Charles de Gaulle, Lycée International de Londres Winston Churchill, CFBL as well as leading English schools.
The classes are intentionally kept small so that each child can be given the individual attention they require. We provide your children with the best foundation for secondary school.
Fully Accredited Bilingual Education since 1983
La Petite Ecole Française is an independent English/French Bilingual school that follows the French national education system as well as the British national curriculum (literacy, reading and writing). The school is part of the AEFE (Agence pour l’Enseignement Français à l’Etranger) and its students progress to French and English schools.
PEF has been awarded French Education Nationale ‘Homologation’ status for all its levels from Petite Section (Nursery) to CM2 (Year 6). The ‘Homologation’ is a special accreditation given by the French Ministry of Education.
Encouraging development
Great Location and Modern Facilities
Wonderful Community of Parents
We have a diverse, international community of parents who are very involved in the school. Each class has two parent representatives, who meet every half term with the Headteacher.
We greatly value the suggestions of all the parents and the school benefits from their feedback. Parents are actively involved in outings, volunteering for big events such as sports day or the school ‘fete’.
We also encourage parents to come to the school to read books, talk about their culture, jobs and so on. All communication from the school to families is in both English and French.
Welcome From the Headteacher
Welcome to La Petite Ecole Française, where bilingual learning comes to life in a warm, inclusive and vibrant community.
It is with great pleasure that I take on the role of headteacher and build upon the excellent work being done at the school. La Petite Ecole Française offers a joyful, balanced and academically rigorous bilingual education in a caring community setting. Rooted in both the French and British traditions, our approach celebrates curiosity, creativity and personal growth. We keep class sizes small so that every child is known, supported and challenged at just the right level.
Children thrive when they feel secure, inspired and seen. At La Petite Ecole Française, we place strong relationships at the heart of learning, between staff, children and families. Our dedicated team nurtures each child’s confidence, independence and love of learning, preparing them not only for academic success but also for life beyond the classroom.
Whether you are new to our school or already part of our community, I look forward to meeting you and working together to give your child the best possible start.
Anthony Artist Headteacher

Sport Activities
Bilingual French/English School in London
Nursery and Primary open for all
La Petite Ecole Française
Sport Activities
Sport activities are an important part of the French curriculum and are also essential to help children develop their motor and social skills.
From Petite to Grande Section, sport sessions are organized in the large gymnasium, next to the school with two sessions per week for each class. In addition, sports classes also take place in the school hall or in the playground on other days of the week. Teachers and assistants aim to develop motor skills using a motor-skills circuit with different equipment which the children can walk on, jump over, roll on etc. They organise games with the pupils which develop their co-operation skills. The Maternelle pupils have 30 minutes of dance per week where they learn ballet. Please refer to the ‘Dance and Music’ section for more information.
In Primaire (CP to CM2), pupils do a different activity each term; tennis, climbing and swimming. They enjoy climbing and playing tennis at the Westway Sports Centre and swimming at the Kensington Leisure Centre. All the activities are lead by professional coaches based at the Sport Centres.

La Petite Ecole Française is registered for 190 children. At the start of the school year the children must have reached the age of 2 years or older. The school has never discriminated against and has no intention of discriminating against any child on the grounds of sex, race, religion or ethnicity in its admissions policy.
We conduct regular school visits for parents. If you are interested, please contact the school office on +44 (0) 208 960 1278.
Step 1: Download the Application Form
Application forms should be emailed to the school (admin@lapef.co.uk) together with a registration fee of £120 paid by bank transfer with the child’s name on it. Please scan and send the application form by email and we will send you our bank details.
Step 2: Deposit
If your child is offered a place, the deposit and admin fee must be paid prior to the child starting the school. The admin fee will only be charged if the child is offered a place at the school and the place is accepted by the parents.
The deposit is held by the school and returned to the parent when the child leaves the school, provided a full term’s notice is given. Therefore, if a parent wishes to remove their child from the school, a full term’s notice has to be given in writing in order for the deposit to be returned.
For example, if a child leaves the school in January, the deposit will only be returned if written notice is given to the school before September. If the school fees increase the deposit may increase.
HOw much does it cost?
School Fees
The school fees must be paid within the first week of the term commencing. The preferred payment method is by bank transfer; however, a cheque will also be accepted. Please remember to quote the child’s name on the back of the cheque or as a reference in the case of a bank transfer. Cheques are payable to ‘La Petite Ecole Francaise’.

**Includes hot lunch and dessert four days per week. Non-vegetarian and vegetarian options only.
Early Years Funding
Pupils that are 2-4 years old may be entitled to the Early Years Education Entitlement (Early Years Funding), which is provided by the local authority. Please call the school office for more information. It is available for all parents unless the fees are paid by the employer.
